zh.title: 如果地球不一样？
zh.intro: 先改一个条件，再到真实星球寻找相似处与差别。带着观察返回地球。

questions.distance: 如果地球离太阳更近，或更远？
questions.worlds: 真实星球，和我们的实验一样吗？
questions.atmosphere: 距离不变，空气怎样改变热量的散出？
questions.return: 回到地球：哪些差异已经能解释？
questions.tilt: 如果地球不倾斜，或者倾斜更多？

observations.distance: 移动距离，比较地球接收的阳光。地表图只帮助辨认同一颗地球，不是温度或气候地图。
observations.worlds: 选择一个真实世界，跟着同一个地面标记下降，再观察那里。真实世界的条件不会被实验旋钮修改。
observations.atmosphere: 保留刚才的太阳距离，只调节向外热辐射的有效散出系数。比较同一参考温度下，吸收与散出的热量。
observations.return: 这里重新观察真实地球；你的假设距离、大气旋钮和各星球观察位置仍保留着。
observations.tilt: 保留同一个地点，比较不倾斜与所选倾角的白昼长短，再转动地球观察同一处日照。

zh.hypothesis: 假设实验 · 地球参照
zh.real: 真实世界 · 有依据的示意
zh.au: 地球平均距日距离 = 1 AU
zh.distanceHeld: 固定：太阳光度、反照率与热辐射散出系数。圆轨道参照位置，不是把真实地球瞬间推入另一条轨道。
zh.escapeHeld: 固定：当前太阳距离与反照率。这个教学系数概括向太空散出热辐射的效率，不是气压或气体浓度。
zh.warming: 吸收较多，最初趋向升温
zh.cooling: 散出较多，最初趋向降温
zh.balanced: 在这个模型中收支平衡
zh.balanceNote: 两条带使用同一线性标尺，单位 W/m²，按整球表面积平均。散出带固定使用出发时的模型温度；不是调节后的平衡值。
zh.sceneLabel: 可拖动与键盘观察的星球；加减键缩放
zh.failed: 三维画面暂不可用。实验读数、地点说明、路线和资料仍可使用。
zh.loading: 正在准备同一颗星球的观察画面…
zh.sceneBoundary: 各世界单独取景，不能从屏幕大小比较真实直径。下降是观察镜头移动，不是自由落体、测得高度或可生存的飞行。地形为指定区域的教学重建，不是实测地形。
zh.sectionBoundary: 剖面依据观测与材料模型推断，层厚为示意；可操作的三维图不等于直接看见了内部。
zh.moreWorld: 继续深入这个真实世界
zh.moreAir: 走近真实大气的分层与现象
zh.entry: 从地球出发：如果距离和空气不同？
zh.actualNote: 这些是独立资料中的取整代表值，不是本实验的预测，也不表示每个地点和时刻都相同。

worldNotes.venus: 金星的浓厚大气和云层也参与热量收支。接近时先看云幕，地面是有依据的重建；把实验地球移到这里不会自动变成金星。
worldNotes.mars: 火星今天的大气很稀薄，地表有明确的区域与季节差异。比较气压与地貌，不能只用距日距离解释它的全部环境。
worldNotes.earth: 地球是我们的固定参照。看见云和海洋之后，继续追问热量怎样进入、怎样离开；画面不是实时天气。
worldNotes.uranus: 天王星的倾角接近98°，季节受光极端，但它也是远离太阳的冰巨星。没有可供降落的固体表面，不能把它当成只改了倾角的地球。

zh.formula: 固定太阳光度：S = 1361/r²；整球平均吸收 Q = S(1 − A)/4；平衡满足 eσT⁴ = Q。r 的单位是 AU，A = 0.30，σ 为斯特藩–玻尔兹曼常数，e 为有效散出系数。出发值 e = 0.61 使模型大致接近现代地球的全球平均温度，但不是气候参数反演。
zh.limitations: 这是固定反照率、均匀温度的零维灰体教学模型。不计算天气、昼夜、云反馈、冰反馈、海洋热储存或调整所需时间；不能用它预测真实金星、火星、海岸线、液态水或生命。增加温室气体通常会改变热辐射；增加空气或云并不只有单一保温作用。
zh.summaryText: 距离改变阳光输入，大气还会影响热量散出；真实世界同时有多种差异。一个旋钮能帮助分辨机制，不能复刻整个星球。
zh.saved: 距离和大气旋钮已保留；再次访问金星或火星，会回到各自保存的地点与观察进度。
zh.deeper: 继续研究脚下与地球的历史
zh.rulerNote: 距离沿同一线性标尺；太阳和地球的圆点是放大的定位标记，不代表直径。
zh.tiltEntry: 下一条 if：如果地轴倾斜不同？
zh.tiltReadingsTitle: 同一地点、同一轨道位置
zh.tiltHeld: 固定：圆轨道、1 AU、地球的自转周期。地点和轨道位置是观察选择；倾角是本实验改变的条件。画面停在所选地点的地方太阳正午。
zh.tiltBoundary: 青色线是地轴，金色圈是赤道，亮圈标出所选地点。地面标记、太阳方向与读数共用四季专题的几何。高倾角地球仍是反事实实验，不等于具有天王星的组成、距离或气候。
zh.tiltFormula: 采用原有四季模型：δ = asin(sin ε · sin λ)。ε 为倾角，λ 为春分起算的轨道相位；结合所选纬度计算地方正午太阳高度和理想昼长。相同的太阳方向用于三维地球，换镜头不改变日照状态。
zh.tiltLimitations: 这是圆轨道、点太阳的日照几何，不计算温度、天气、折射或真实日出。零倾角时圆轨道模型没有倾角造成的季节日照差异；真实偏心轨道仍可能产生年内受光变化。天王星的比较不把地球的一年当成天王星的一年。
zh.tiltWorldQuestion: 倾角相似，真实世界还多了哪些不同条件？
zh.tiltWorldObservation: 先保留刚才实验的地点和季节，再观察天王星或其他真实世界。到云层近景时，不会出现供降落的固体地板。
zh.tiltWorldNext: 带着季节问题返回地球
zh.tiltReturnText: 倾角改变阳光在纬度和季节间的分布；真实天王星还具有不同的距离、组成与公转周期。返回实验，比较同一地点在不同季节的日照。
zh.moreSeasons: 继续研究地球的昼夜与四季
zh.gasBoundary: 各世界单独取景，屏幕大小不比较真实直径。镜头接近巨行星云层，不是降落、自由落体或可生存飞行。云层和内部几何为教学示意，不增加固体地面。
zh.tiltAgain: 再比较一次地轴与季节

en.title: What if Earth were different?
en.intro: Change one condition, compare it with real worlds, then bring your observations back to Earth.

questions.distance: What if Earth were closer to, or farther from, the Sun?
questions.worlds: Are real worlds the same as our experiment?
questions.atmosphere: At the same distance, how does air affect heat escaping?
questions.return: Back on Earth: which differences can we explain?
questions.tilt: What if Earth had no tilt, or much more tilt?

observations.distance: Change the distance and compare incoming sunlight. The surface image identifies the same Earth; it is not a temperature or climate map.
observations.worlds: Choose a real world. Follow the same ground marker down and inspect that region. Experiment controls never change the real world's conditions.
observations.atmosphere: Keep your chosen solar distance. Change only an effective infrared escape factor and compare absorbed and outgoing energy at the same reference temperature.
observations.return: You are observing real Earth again. Your hypothetical distance, atmosphere control and observations of each world are still saved.
observations.tilt: Keep the same place. Compare daylight at zero and selected tilt, then turn the Earth to inspect the same illumination.

en.distanceHeld: Fixed: solar luminosity, albedo and infrared escape factor. This is a circular-orbit reference position, not an instantaneous push of real Earth into a new orbit.
en.escapeHeld: Fixed: your current solar distance and albedo. This teaching factor summarizes infrared escape to space; it is not air pressure or gas concentration.
en.outgoing: Outgoing at the same reference temperature
en.warming: More absorbed: initially tends to warm
en.cooling: More outgoing: initially tends to cool
en.balanceNote: Both bands share one linear scale in W/m², averaged over the whole sphere. The outgoing band uses the starting model temperature, not the new equilibrium temperature.
en.sceneLabel: Drag or use arrow keys to inspect the world; plus and minus zoom
en.failed: The 3D view is unavailable. Experiment readings, site descriptions, navigation and sources still work.
en.loading: Preparing the same world's observation view…
en.sceneBoundary: Worlds are framed separately; screen size does not compare actual diameters. Approach moves an observation camera, not free fall, measured altitude or survivable flight. Terrain is a teaching reconstruction of the named region, not a measured elevation map.
en.sectionBoundary: Cutaways are inferred from observations and material models; layer thicknesses are schematic. A manipulable 3D view does not directly reveal the interior.
en.moreAir: Inspect real atmospheric structure and phenomena
en.back: Return to the saved Earth experiment
en.entry: Start from Earth: what if distance and air were different?
en.actualNote: These are rounded representative values from independent references, not predictions from this experiment or conditions at every place and time.

worldNotes.venus: Venus's dense atmosphere and clouds also affect its energy balance. Approach through the cloud cover; the ground is an evidence-based reconstruction. Moving experimental Earth here does not turn it into Venus.
worldNotes.mars: Mars today has a thin atmosphere and distinct regional and seasonal conditions. Compare pressure and terrain: solar distance alone does not explain its entire environment.
worldNotes.earth: Earth remains our reference. After noticing clouds and oceans, ask how energy enters and leaves. The image is not live weather.
worldNotes.uranus: Uranus is tilted by nearly 98°, producing extreme seasonal illumination. It is also a distant ice giant with no solid landing surface, not Earth with only its tilt changed.

en.formula: Fixed solar luminosity: S = 1361/r²; whole-sphere mean absorption Q = S(1 − A)/4; equilibrium requires eσT⁴ = Q. r is in AU, A = 0.30, σ is the Stefan–Boltzmann constant, and e is an effective escape factor. The starting e = 0.61 puts the model near modern Earth's global mean temperature; it is not a climate-parameter retrieval.
en.limitations: This zero-dimensional grey model assumes fixed albedo and uniform temperature. It does not calculate weather, day and night, cloud or ice feedbacks, ocean heat storage, or adjustment time. It cannot predict actual Venus, Mars, coastlines, liquid water or life. More greenhouse gas generally changes infrared transfer; more air or cloud does not have only one insulating effect.
en.summaryText: Distance changes incoming sunlight; air also affects outgoing heat. Real worlds differ in several conditions at once. One control helps isolate a mechanism; it cannot reproduce an entire planet.
en.saved: Distance and the atmosphere control are retained. Revisit Venus or Mars to recover each world's saved site and observation progress.
en.deeper: Explore Earth's ground and history further
en.rulerNote: Distances share one linear ruler. Sun and Earth dots are enlarged position markers, not diameters.
en.tiltEntry: Next what-if: change the axial tilt
en.tiltHeld: Fixed: circular orbit, 1 AU and Earth's rotation period. Place and orbital position choose the observation; tilt is the changed condition. The scene is at local solar noon for the selected place.
en.tiltBoundary: The cyan line is the axis, the gold circle is the equator, and a bright ring marks the selected place. The marker, sunlight and readings share the Seasons geometry. A highly tilted Earth remains hypothetical; it does not acquire Uranus's composition, distance or climate.
en.tiltFormula: The existing Seasons model gives δ = asin(sin ε · sin λ). ε is axial tilt and λ is orbital phase from the spring equinox. The selected latitude gives local-noon altitude and ideal daylight duration. The same solar direction lights the 3D Earth; moving the camera does not change illumination.
en.tiltLimitations: This is point-Sun geometry on a circular orbit, not temperature, weather, refraction or a sunrise forecast. At zero tilt this model has no tilt-driven seasonal sunlight difference; real orbital eccentricity may still produce annual changes in incoming light. Comparing Uranus does not make an Earth year equal to a Uranian year.
en.tiltWorldQuestion: With a similar tilt, what other conditions differ on real worlds?
en.tiltWorldObservation: Retain the experimental place and season while inspecting Uranus or other real worlds. A cloud close-up does not acquire a solid landing floor.
en.tiltWorldNext: Bring the seasonal question back to Earth
en.tiltReturnText: Tilt changes how sunlight is distributed across latitudes and seasons. Real Uranus also differs in distance, composition and orbital period. Return to the experiment to compare seasons at the same place.
en.moreSeasons: Explore Earth's day, night and seasons further
en.gasBoundary: Worlds are framed separately; screen size does not compare actual diameters. The camera approaches giant-planet clouds, not landing, free fall or survivable flight. Clouds and interiors are teaching illustrations; no solid landing surface is added.
